mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-over-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility, culminating in a significant jump at t-0w, indicates a sustained recovery trend in consumer activity that will continue to drive retail and recreation visits higher over the next four weeks.

candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 20% and maintains a downward trend
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decline or stabilize below 20%, but RETAIL_REC mobility decreases over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous and consistent upward trend in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility suggests a strong return to office-based work and associated commuting patterns. candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show week-on-week increases for at least two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: Both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility continue to increase, but RETAIL_REC mobility declines over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based recovery across all out-of-home categories (RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES) indicates an active and effective policy-driven reopening phase. This momentum, likely supported by easing restrictions, will continue to lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as more businesses fully operate.
failure_condition: Despite continued increases in other out-of-home categories, RETAIL_REC mobility stagnates or declines over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The significant week-on-week increase in PARKS mobility from t-1w to t-0w (from -37.3 to -29.6) signals a surge in outdoor leisure activities. This heightened engagement in public spaces will directly translate to increased general recreation and retail spending in the immediate next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility increases by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility increases by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC mobility declines in the subsequent week.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility over the last four weeks indicates a sustained shift in daily patterns, with individuals spending less time at home. candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility shows a consistent decline for at least two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility continues its downward trend, but RETAIL_REC mobility decreases over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combined upward momentum observed across WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and PARKS mobility signifies a broad and accelerating return to pre-pandemic routines, encompassing both work and leisure. This widespread increase in public activity creates a highly favorable environment for retail and recreation, driving RETAIL_REC significantly higher over the next four weeks.
